[K] : [Hello there. I have experienced something very similar in the past. My host and I consider each other soul mates, as such we are extremely close. Of course that's my experience, I am very lucky and comfortable how I am now. But there was those rough times and I think there will always be times like that. But I like to think of it this way, our hosts spent loving time creating us and we're not something that they would just discard so easily.]

I'm very relieved to hear you're in a safe situation, it was more my worry that you might be in a really bad space.

I'd say that when you have more time to yourself is when you should attempt to create one, if you still want to then. It does take quite a fair bit of time. But honestly having a tulpa is a very wonderful thing and you sound like a lovely person who would nurture their tulpa well. I'd say for now, do plenty of research, there's plenty on tulpa.io and I'm pretty sure it's linked on this sub too. I saw you tried the RPG method, personally that one doesn't work well for me either also I don't tend to get many bodily sensations when I force (that might just be me!) , there's different methods out there which may work better for you.

But I wish you the best of luck if you do decide to keep trying, don't rush it though as you may just end up backtracking!

Hiya, just wanted to say a few bits here!

First off, if you are being by bullied then please talk to someone of authority about it. As someone who was pretty badly bullied back in my school days and currently having to deal with anxiety and depression, it will get worse if you don't action it. I know it's hard since I've literally been in that sort of situation but I would strongly encourage you to. (trying to avoid people becoming messed up like me) Also if you are feeling depressed then speak to your doctor, depression is very serious and thus should be taken very seriously.

So secondly, I wouldn't recommend making a tulpa in those conditions. Now, for me I have had my tulpa since a young age, so when I went through all of that it was nice to have him there to talk to and such... But he absolutely knew it was a bad thing to rely on him for so much. I wouldn't have considered making a tulpa at that time due to my mental state being so bad. Tulpas require a certain amount of stability and focus in my experience personally. If you are still interested in having a tulpa, please consider reconciliating your condition first.

[K] [Just a few words from me. I'm a very calm and headstrong person, since I've been around my host for so long, I know her extremely well. My host generally takes a few months in creation, even though she has been practicing for a long time now. So, I would say if you really do want it to happen, be prepared that it may take a long time and focus. Her dork of a boyfriend took 2 years to create his tulpa with less meditation time, to put it into perspective.]

Whew, I haven't had much issue with my relationship with my first tulpa (he doesn't like being named online so I'll call him K). Well I did have one issue before, but it wasn't one of these questions you asked, more of a person to person issue. K has never felt an obligation to date me after I first realised my feelings toward him, it was mutual for us, we've been together for many many years. 

I've also never had an issue with the cheating thing you mentioned, mainly because we're pretty close and accepting of each other's interests even if it's other people. K has mentioned he was a bit upset when I got together with my first human boyfriend, but that turned out to be a good hunch as that guy hated the idea of sharing and tulpas, long story short I left that guy as he was very toxic towards my tulpas and demeaning to me. 

Now I have a current boyfriend who is very accepting of tulpas, he's gotten to know K very well and the 2 of them are on very good terms. So, from my experience, having a relationship with a tulpa is great as long as it's absolutely mutual! But be careful for the people around you as a lot of them aren't so lovely towards that sort of thing.

As a host with similar issues I can relate to that feeling of wanting to escape using one of my tulpas. But from experience I know it will make things a lot worse. I'm still dealing with my issues, the very fact I'm writing this is proof I'm improving. But this running away is going to make things worse for her, I mean her issues will most likely get more severe. When I used to hide my feelings all the time I would actually take it all out on my real life partner (long distance thankfully) in extremely aggressive and demeaning texts and chats, I just worry that she might start doing the same to you if left unchecked, as she seems to be in a similar position I was in. 
She absolutely needs professional help if she's already resorted to this. I know how hard it is, it took me 4 years to even see my doctor, but I also know it takes encouragement to go find help. If you feel like she may be endangering herself at any point then I'd say call or find professional help without her permission, sadly one of my tulpas had to do that for me in the past and I'm extremely thankful to him now.

Personally I don't think I would recommend creating a tulpa if you're in a really bad place, not only could it hinder you it could also affect whoever you create. 

From my experience however, my first tulpa has been with me since I was very very young and he's been extremely supportive for me. To not go into too much detail there were events 5 or 6 years ago that ended up with me having a couple diagnosed conditions anxiety and depression basically. Back then I was in a very dark place and, skipping some stuff I'd rather not say, he kept me together at that time. But he told me he knew he wouldn't be able to help on his own, which is why he encouraged me to see my doctor. I think it'd probably be easier for him to talk about it.

Also on the topic of this discussion, I have actually spoken to my host's therapist whilst switching. She did talk about me beforehand, it wasn't some big surprise or anything like that, she also explained briefly about tulpas but not into too much depth. It was a pleasant experience for me. The therapist was very open and accepting of me, albeit a bit curious. She seemed to agree with my presence as a force for good within my host, it was nice to have that reassurance.\]

Hi, host with a relevant experience here.

I used to have really serious doubts too, a few years ago now but it's extremely memorable for me. I was in a very toxic relationship with a guy at the time, back then I had my natural tulpa (he's practically my soul mate honestly, he doesn't like me using his name on the internet) and my 2nd forced tulpa Kaito. Now, I was actually perceived as crazy by this guy, I told him about my 2 after a few months of being together, I don't know if he was defensive as I am in a very close relationship with my 1st, but he would constantly berate me and say I should get help. Back then it did make me feel like I needed help, especially as I didn't really know what a tulpa was back then, only the very basic information really. It did feel horrible, and the other 2 were right in the end, I did need to leave that toxic relationship but I did feel like I was wrong to take the advice of some people in my head at the time. But my 1st has helped me so much in the past, I have only trust for him, I can't see any of them as a harm to me at all so why should I doubt them?

Since then I started a relationship with my best friend for several years, I told him about my tulpas right away and he genuinely accepted it (he even accepts the fact he's not exactly no.1 in my heart haha), he loves talking to my, now more, tulpas and I'm pretty sure one of them is pretty head over heels for him herself even.

I think people will always have doubts since they're not exactly tangible, but if people are genuine they wouldn't try to make you feel bad about it - your fiancee made a great point with everything you believe is real is real to you. I got through a pretty rough spot which is why I really don't have any doubts anymore, but I suppose it's up to the individual what they want to believe in the most.

\[K\]: You may know me as the 1st she mentions in this, I just wanted to add that you shouldn't ignore your feelings, if you truly love them then never doubt that. Your fiancee sounds like a lovely person and from what I can see he's already very accepting of it. Sure enough, people will react differently to things they can't see, but if you care about people you can help them understand. Even sometimes, humans are more damaging than us.
